alert.nmos.registre_bascule: NMOS registry {mort} unreachable — failing over to {url}
alert.nmos.registre_decouvert: NMOS registry discovered on the network: {url}
alert.nmos.registre_perdu: NMOS registry {url} unreachable, and no other announced on the network
service.nmos.activation_is_05_auto_des_s: Automatic IS-05 activation of remote senders
service.nmos.annonce_la_source_dans_les_: Announces the source in the 2110 engine's TX SDPs → the receiver performs an IGMPv3 SSM (S,G) join. Recommended on an SSM-capable fabric (PIM-SSM / NBM). Uncheck on a plain IGMP-snooping L2 switch: the (S,G) join is registered there but never forwarded (a silent 0 Mbps) — without the line, the receiver falls back to a (*,G) join, which is delivered. Applied at the engine's redeploy.
service.nmos.automatique_chaque_conteneu: Automatic — each container auto-creates its Rx/Tx
service.nmos.c_est_l_uuid_du_node_la_bcp: This is the Node's UUID. The BCP requires the manufacturer + product + instance triplet to be unique; making it editable would amount to offering to make it ambiguous.
service.nmos.ce_que_voit_l_ingenieur_d_e: What the operations engineer sees when an IS-04 query returns several devices under the same label. These three values are published as tags on the Node and on the Device, plus the function on the Device. They also feed IS-12's NcDeviceManager — one single source, so that the two protocols do not describe two different devices.
service.nmos.certains_devices_2110_conve: Some 2110 devices (SDI→IP converters) expose a genuine NMOS IS-04/05 API but emit nothing until their own sender has received the IS-05 activation PATCH (master_enable) — standard NMOS behaviour, not proprietary. When enabled, an RX subscription (SDP pasted by hand, with no shared registry) triggers mDNS discovery of the source device's node and activates its sender if needed. Best-effort, with no impact if the device exposes no NMOS node.
service.nmos.chaque_conteneur_sert_son_n: Each container serves its own Node
service.nmos.cree_un_pool_de_rx_tx_fixes: Creates a pool of fixed Rx/Tx, then cables a 2110 container channel by channel (video, audio, ANC together) in one click. Ideal in static mode.
service.nmos.en_statique_un_conteneur_21: In static mode, a 2110 container exposes no NMOS resource until its slots are cabled to fixed Rx/Tx from the pool (below) — a stable NMOS identity across project recall and across nodes.
service.nmos.endpoints_exposes_sous_x_nm: Endpoints exposed under /x-nmos/node/v1.3/ and /x-nmos/connection/v1.1/. The Node plus its Devices and Receivers are registered with the configured RDS, with a 5 s heartbeat.
service.nmos.etendre_une_selection_video: Extend a video selection to the audio + ANC of the same channel (Rx)
service.nmos.filtre_de_source_ssm_dans_l: SSM source filter in the SDPs (a=source-filter)
service.nmos.glisser_un_slot_vers_une_re: Drag a slot onto a resource to cable it (one at a time). Multiple selection: click, Ctrl-click, Shift-click (range), or rubber-band on the background, then “Connect the selection” and click the starting resource. “Assign all” cables every channel of a container. Clicking an edge unbinds it.
service.nmos.inactif_n_est_pas_une_panne: Inactive is not a fault: it is a Receiver with no IS-05 subscription, or an output slot with no requested rate. Content flags (frozen picture, black, silence) only degrade the stream if they are armed on the source (I/O Sources page) — a deliberately frozen test pattern stays healthy.
service.nmos.indispensable_des_qu_un_sec: Essential as soon as a second 2110 engine joins the cluster: without a distinct prefix, two nodes each expose an “Rx 1” that a third-party controller cannot tell apart.
service.nmos.is07.confirmer_suppression: Delete this connection? Its mapping goes with it, and its Receiver disappears from IS-04: a controller that had activated it will see its resource vanish.
service.nmos.is07.conns_intro: A connection = one protocol writing into one level. The URL and the Source to listen to come from the external controller, over IS-05: they are read-only. The “sender Source → our signal” mapping is edited on the Labels page, one column per connection, next to the TSL columns.
service.nmos.is07.intro: IS-07 carries tally events. Outgoing: we publish the state of our signals, one Source per (flow, level). Incoming: an external controller sends us some, and a connection says which level it writes into — exactly like a TSL connection.
service.nmos.is_12_est_le_protocole_de_c: IS-12 is the NMOS control protocol (WebSocket). It publishes one monitor per Receiver and per Sender here, compliant with BCP-008-01/02: link, connection, stream and PTP synchronisation status, counters and cause messages — readable by any third-party controller, with no proprietary API. Read-only: no published object allows routing or starting anything. The endpoint is advertised to controllers in the controls array of the IS-04 Devices.
service.nmos.js.is12_no_provider: IS-12 is running, but the NMOS provider is disabled: no IS-04 resource exists, hence no monitor. Enable the provider above.
service.nmos.js.sans_monitor: {n} IS-04 resource(s) with no 2110 engine behind them
service.nmos.le_meme_modele_qu_is_12_ser: The same model as IS-12, served over REST on the UI's port — for a controller that does not want to hold a WebSocket open. IS-14 additionally brings model backup and restore (bulkProperties): a dry-run validation is possible before applying. Both protocols can run together — the model is built only once.
service.nmos.le_pool_cree_et_l_affectati: the pool created and the assignment apply to this direction
service.nmos.libelles_lt_rx_tx_gt_lt_pre: Labels <Rx|Tx>[_<prefix>]_<ID>_<essence>, zero-padded ID (e.g. Tx_Projet_05_Video; with no prefix → Tx_05_Video). Audio as …_Audio (or …_Audio1/2), ANC as …_Anc.
service.nmos.liste_nmos_de_niveau_cluste: Cluster-level NMOS list: every sender/receiver keeps its UUID whichever container serves it (bound through instance_uuid). A resource served by no container stays exposed (orphan, inactive) — the controller's routing survives. Relabelling is persistent; an orphan can be deleted, or one can be created ahead of time.
service.nmos.meta_conteneurs: The first makes every container serve its own Node API from its agent — it requires an up-to-date bobi-compute image; older containers ignore it without error. The second publishes plugin parameters and actions as a control model: that is a contract controllers memorise, and the authority key will change once the IEEE CID is granted. The third opens a session to every registered third-party device and turns its status changes into alerts here.
service.nmos.meta_is07: Publishes the tally of TSL-mapped flows as NMOS events, as an off / red / green / amber enumeration — the LH, RH and TT levels are published as they are, without presuming which one means “on air”. Without the WebSocket transport a controller polls the state; with it, it subscribes and receives changes. The Sender is only advertised when the transport is actually served.
service.nmos.meta_is09: Publishes the facility PTP domain, heartbeat interval and syslog collector so a third-party device can align with them. Same caution as the registry: priority 100 means development. In the other direction we read a host facility's System API and raise an alert on a PTP domain mismatch — never reconfiguring anything.
service.nmos.meta_mxl: Publishes the internal graph (mixer, multiview, streamer, 2110 engine ports) as NMOS resources, transport urn:x-nmos:transport:mxl. Writing is closed: cabling goes through the Cables page, and an IS-05 PATCH is refused with 405. Opening it lets a third-party controller re-cable production — keep it for trials. ⚠ This transport is not yet in the AMWA register: a strict controller may reject these resources.
service.nmos.meta_redemarrage: Toggles take effect immediately, except those that open a server (IS-07 WebSocket transport, DNS-SD-advertised registry): those need a service restart.
service.nmos.meta_registre: Lets a third-party device register with us and appear in the inventory. A Node that stops heartbeating is removed, together with its resources, after the given delay. Priority defaults to 100 = “development” in IS-04 terms: a strict controller IGNORES the registry until it is lowered to 0–99 — but lowering it diverts devices away from a registry already in place on the same network.
service.nmos.port_distinct_de_l_ui_5000_: A port separate from the UI (5000): the orchestrator's server cannot upgrade an HTTP connection to a WebSocket, and the IS-12 spec precisely provides for a separate URL. Remember the controller's firewall.
service.nmos.prefixe_par_nud_vide_herite: Per-node prefix (empty = inherits the global one)
service.nmos.publier_le_bus_mxl_en_nmos: Publish the MXL bus over NMOS
service.nmos.reimporte_un_fichier_export: Re-imports an exported file keeping the UUIDs (does not break NMOS routing)
service.nmos.statique_pool_fixe_on_cable: Static — fixed pool, containers are cabled
service.nmos.supprime_d_abord_les_ressou: First deletes the pool resources missing from the file/snapshot
service.nmos.supprime_les_rx_tx_auto_cre: Deletes the auto-created Rx/Tx of containers that are gone (keeps the fixed pool, the served ones and the subscribed ones)
service.nmos.telecharge_le_pool_les_bind: Downloads the pool + the bindings + the mode as JSON (UUIDs included)
service.nmos.vide_rx_1_video_tx_1_anc_av: Empty → Rx 1 (video), Tx 1 (anc). With REGIE-A → REGIE-A Rx 1 (video). It changes neither the NMOS UUIDs, nor the MXL flows, nor the SSRCs — no subscription has to be redone. This prefix does, however, also seed the natural groups (BCP-002-01): those are frozen when each resource is created and will therefore NOT follow a prefix change — that is intended, the NMOS registry requires a group to be immutable (a controller builds its production naming from it and never asks again). Resources created after the change do carry the new prefix.
service.nmos.vide_tout_le_registre_nmos_: Empties the whole NMOS registry (pool included) plus the cabling. The UUIDs are lost.
